articles.title: Boundedness of Riesz potentials in weighted variable exponent Lebesgue spaces
articles.abstract: In this paper, we study the boundedness of Riesz potentials in weighted variable exponent Lebesgue spaces. We establish necessary and sufficient conditions for the boundedness of the Riesz potential operator in these spaces, extending previous results to the variable exponent setting with Muckenhoupt weights.
articles.content:
## Introduction

Riesz potentials play a fundamental role in harmonic analysis and potential theory. The boundedness of Riesz potentials in Lebesgue spaces with variable exponent has attracted considerable attention in recent years.

## Main Results

We establish the following main results:
1. A characterization of the boundedness of Riesz potentials in weighted variable exponent Lebesgue spaces
2. The sharpness of the conditions obtained
3. Applications to Sobolev-type inequalities

## Key Theorem

**Theorem 1.** Let $p(\cdot)$ be a variable exponent satisfying the log-H\"older condition, and let $w$ be a Muckenhoupt weight. Then the Riesz potential operator $I_\alpha$ is bounded from $L^{p(\cdot)}(w)$ to $L^{q(\cdot)}(w)$ if and only if certain integral conditions hold.

articles.title: Wolff potentials and their applications to nonlinear elliptic equations
articles.abstract: We investigate the properties of Wolff potentials in the context of nonlinear elliptic equations. Our results provide new insights into the regularity of solutions to quasilinear elliptic equations with measure data, extending the classical potential-theoretic approach to more general nonlinear settings.
articles.content:
## Introduction

Wolff potentials are fundamental tools in the study of nonlinear potential theory and its applications to partial differential equations. This paper aims to deepen our understanding of Wolff potentials and their role in the regularity theory of nonlinear elliptic equations.

## Main Results

We obtain:
1. Sharp estimates for Wolff potentials in various function spaces
2. Applications to the regularity of solutions to $p$-Laplace type equations
3. Pointwise estimates for solutions via Wolff potentials

articles.title: On the regularity of free boundaries in elliptic Bernoulli-type problems
articles.abstract: This paper studies the regularity of free boundaries in elliptic Bernoulli-type problems. We establish optimal regularity results for the free boundary under minimal assumptions, contributing to the understanding of singularities in free boundary problems.
articles.content:
## Introduction

Bernoulli-type free boundary problems arise in various physical contexts, including fluid dynamics, combustion theory, and electrochemistry. The study of free boundary regularity is a central topic in the theory of free boundary problems.

## Main Results

We prove:
1. Optimal regularity of the free boundary under the assumption of flatness
2. A classification of possible singularities
3. New monotonicity formulas for Bernoulli-type functionals

articles.title: Harmonic analysis techniques in potential theory: a survey
articles.abstract: This survey provides an overview of harmonic analysis techniques used in modern potential theory. We cover topics including Calder\'on-Zygmund theory, weighted norm inequalities, and their applications to the study of Riesz and Wolff potentials.
articles.content:
## Introduction

Harmonic analysis and potential theory have deep interconnections. This survey aims to present a comprehensive overview of the harmonic analysis techniques that have proven essential in the development of modern potential theory.

## Topics Covered

1. Calder\'on-Zygmund theory and its applications
2. Weighted norm inequalities and Muckenhoupt weights
3. Riesz and Wolff potentials: recent developments
4. Applications to PDEs and free boundary problems
